summary: Walk through the text one run at a time: from the run's start, move forward while the character stays the same, then write the character and the run length (T6 — runs / streaks).

blocks.title: Read the text
blocks.text: `.strip()` removes stray spaces at the ends so they don't become a run.

blocks.title: Output pieces and a start index
blocks.text: `out` collects pieces like `'a3'`; `i` is where the current run starts.

blocks.title: Walk to the end of this run
blocks.text: `j` moves right while it sees the same character as `s[i]`. `j < len(s)` is checked first so `s[j]` never runs past the end. When the loop stops, `j` is the first character of the NEXT run.

blocks.title: Write the run and jump
blocks.text: The run length is `j - i`; an f-string writes it in full, so a run of 12 becomes `z12` (not `z1` + `2`). Then `i = j` jumps straight to the next run.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 1000 — each character is visited once by `j`.
pitfalls: Forgetting the last run (common with a `for` loop that only writes when the character changes).
Assuming run lengths are a single digit.
